title: Hemorath
subtitle: The First Saint
text: The first of the Harbingers, working before there was an Order to name him. Hemorath found that he could draw blood out of other living things and harden its iron at will: Animus and Ferric, the two tendencies still read in his remains. Every measure he took made him stronger, so he kept taking, long past need, until his flesh split and died around the blood. His marrow never stopped. It still makes blood faster than his ruined vessels can hold, and pulls what it lacks from anything alive nearby. His successors walled him in stone, with basins to meter what he could reach, and he dried to the tall, sunken, iron-stiff figure in the sarcophagus. Roused, he drinks the blood cast against him and grows stronger for it. Pour in more than the marrow can carry and he bursts, exsanguinated. The marrow begins refilling him before the lid has closed, and in time he wakes hungry again. Keep beyond the blood-drawing ring when his claw rises. Blood leaks from his ruined vessels, so forcing an overload means feeding him faster than he empties. His close presence drains active blood; with nothing left to draw, the marrow tears at living flesh instead. His iron patches rise before an Iron Rake marks three parallel lanes. Step into the gaps. A wider warning announces Marrow Rupture: leave its reach or jump the outward-moving wave of blood.
